title: How to Make a 120dB Emergency Whistle & 10km Solar Signal Mirror from an Empty Beverage Can and Mirror
threatLevelText: [3,000Hz Acoustic Resonance & 10km Specular Solar Reflection Rescue Signaling Engineering]
summary: If you already have a commercial pealess rescue whistle, aviation signal mirror, portable air horn, or Personal Locator Beacon (PLB) in your emergency pack or life vest, always use that ready-made gear first for the fastest rescue. However, when trapped under collapsed building rubble or stranded in floods or mountains without gear, shouting at the top of your lungs only reaches 80–85dB and ruins your vocal cords and stamina within 15 minutes. By folding a discarded beverage can (or tin lid), you can craft a resonance whistle that produces a piercing 3,000Hz, 115–120dB blast using minimal breath, cutting through storm and rubble noise up to 1.5–2km away. During daylight, pairing a small mirror, switched-off smartphone screen, or kitchen foil left over from a [No-Power Cardboard Thermal Capsule](/protocol-22) with a V-finger sight lets you aim SOS sun flashes at search helicopters 10–15km away.
timeRequired: 10 mins for emergency whistle / 3 mins for solar reflector setup
successRate: 99% (when cut edges are stone-ground, 2–3mm sound window is aligned, side holes are finger-sealed, and V-finger sight is aligned)
difficulty: Beginner (Crafted immediately from an empty beverage can, rough stone, and mirror/dark phone screen/foil without special tools)
outputPerHour: Amplifies acoustic reach 10x (1.5–2km) over shouting and projects 10–15km daytime optical SOS flashes

materials.name: 1 Empty Beverage Can (or Thin Tin Lid, Firm Bottle Cap, or Hollow Bamboo Stem)
materials.desc: Thin, springy sheet metal that bends easily by hand and vibrates crisply to generate high-frequency sound waves. If using a steel food tin, never heat it in fire since internal epoxy coatings or zinc plating release toxic fumes; cut it cold and tie a [Wild Kudzu Vine Rope](/protocol-05) lanyard so you never drop it.

materials.name: Sharp Stone Flake (or Scissors/Knife) & Rough River Stone or Concrete Chunk for Grinding
materials.desc: Used to score and snap the can wall into clean strips and grind down razor-sharp edges. Without scissors, score a deep groove repeatedly using a [Stone Axe & Sharp Stone Flake](/protocol-04), flex the metal back and forth until it snaps cleanly, and rub the edges against rough stone to protect your lips.

materials.name: Small Hand Mirror for 10km Daylight Signaling (or Switched-Off Smartphone Glass / Flat Foil Board)
materials.desc: A flat reflective surface that bounces sunlight into a tight beam toward distant rescue aircraft or ships. If no mirror is available, use the glossy black glass of a dead smartphone or wrap shiny kitchen foil smoothly over a flat piece of cardboard.

steps.title: Step 1: Cut the Empty Can Wall into a Finger-Width Strip and T-Wing Sheet, then Grind Sharp Edges
steps.description:
1. **Remove Top and Bottom to Flatten the Can Wall**: Pierce around the top rim and bottom dome of an empty beverage can with a [Sharp Stone Flake](/protocol-04) or blade, slice vertically down the cylinder, and press it flat against the ground.
2. **Cut a Finger-Width (1.5cm) Strip and a T-Shape Winged Sheet**: Score lines on the flat sheet to cut **one straight strip 1 finger-joint wide (1.5cm) and 3 joints long (6cm)**, plus a **T-shaped sheet with thumbnail-sized side wings (1cm wide)** at the top.
3. **Score-and-Flex No-Tool Cutting Trick**: When cutting without scissors, do not try to slice through at once; score a deep line with a sharp stone and **fold the metal back and forth 3–4 times** along the line until metal fatigue snaps it straight.
4. **Grind All Cut Edges on Rough Stone**: Freshly cut metal edges have razor-sharp burrs that can slice your lips, so **rub every edge diagonally against a rough river stone or concrete block 20+ times** until completely smooth to the touch.
steps.actionNote: > Why you must never put freshly cut can metal to your mouth without stone grinding: Unfinished metal edges act like razor blades; inhaling or blowing in a panic will deeply lacerate your lips and tongue, causing severe bleeding and infection risk.
svgLabels: Cut can ends & flatten wall into 2 strips
Grind cut edges on stone to protect lips

deepDive.title: Low-Cycle Fatigue Cleavage of Thin Metal Sheets and Oral-Safe Edge Deburring Mechanics
deepDive.text: A 0.1–0.15mm beverage can wall scored with a **0.03mm surface notch** experiences concentrated stress, allowing clean straight-line fracture after just 3–4 reverse bends without scissors. Abrading the resulting micro-burrs against sandstone or concrete (Deburring) ensures both oral safety and smooth laminar airflow inside the windway.

steps.title: Step 2: Fold the Top into a Flat Windway (Fipple) and Roll the Bottom into a Pencil-Thick Sound Chamber
steps.description:
1. **Fold the Top Flat into a Narrow 1mm Windway**: Fold the upper section (or the side wings of the T-sheet) inward to form a **fingernail-thin (approx. 1mm) flat air channel (fipple mouthpiece)** that focuses your breath into a tight jet.
2. **Roll the Bottom Around a Twig into a Pencil-Thick Cylinder**: Place a straight twig **as thick as a pencil or pinky finger (8–10mm diameter)** across the lower tail of the strip and roll the metal tightly around it to form a hollow cylindrical resonance chamber.
3. **Leave a 2–3mm Sound Window Gap**: Position the end of the flat upper windway and the top rim of the lower cylinder so a **rice-grain-sized rectangular opening (2–3mm sound window)** sits directly between them.
4. **Align the Splitting Edge (Labium) with the Air Jet**: Gently press the upper windway with your fingertip so the air jet shooting out of the 1mm slit **strikes the thin metal rim of the cylinder dead-center**, splitting the airflow in half.
steps.actionNote: > Why the whistle only makes a weak hissing sound instead of a piercing shriek: Either the flat windway slit is too wide so your breath scatters, or the outgoing air jet is missing the sharp metal lip of the cylinder instead of striking it head-on.
svgLabels: Fold top flat into a narrow 1mm breath slit
Roll lower tail around twig into cylinder
Set 2-3mm sound gap before cylinder lip
[CORE] Air jet splits on lip for resonance

deepDive.title: Edge-Tone Vortex Shedding and 3,000Hz Acoustic Amplification in Cylindrical Resonators
deepDive.text: When the high-speed air jet exiting the 1mm slit crosses the 2–3mm gap and strikes the sharp cylinder lip (Labium), it oscillates alternately inside and outside the cylinder, creating **Karman vortex shedding**. This rapid oscillation excites the air column inside the 8–10mm chamber, locking into a **2,800–3,200Hz pure tone** where human hearing sensitivity peaks.

steps.title: Step 3: Seal Both Side Holes with Thumb and Index Finger to Blast 120dB International SOS Signals (3 Blasts)
steps.description:
1. **Seal Both Open Cylinder Ends Tightly with Thumb and Index Finger**: Hold the whistle by pressing the soft pads of your **thumb and index finger firmly against both open circular ends** of the rolled cylinder so zero air leaks out the sides.
2. **Optional Hands-Free Seal with Pine Resin or Clay**: If one hand is injured or numb from cold, plug both side holes with carved wooden pegs and seal them airtight using [Pine Resin Waterproof Glue](/protocol-10) or wet clay.
3. **Blow Short and Sharp to Project 120dB High-Frequency Blasts**: Place your lips over the flat windway and blow a crisp, sharp **'TOO!' burst**; the sealed chamber will erupt with an ear-ringing **115–120dB high-frequency whistle blast** audible 1.5–2km away.
4. **Follow the International 3-Blast Distress Cadence**: To save oxygen and distinguish your signal from random noise, repeat the international rescue pattern: **'3 short 1-second blasts ➔ 1 full minute of silence to listen for rescuers'**.
steps.actionNote: > Why no loud whistle sound comes out if you leave the side holes of the cylinder uncovered: If both ends of the rolled cylinder remain open, air pressure and sound waves escape sideways instead of bouncing back and forth inside the chamber to build resonance.
svgLabels: Seal both cylinder ends with thumb & index
Blow short & sharp for 3,000Hz rubble reach

deepDive.title: Closed-End Acoustic Impedance Matching and 3,000Hz Rubble Penetration vs. Stamina Conservation
deepDive.text: Sealing both side openings with finger tissue converts the cylinder into a **closed-end Helmholtz resonator**, boosting sound pressure to **115–120dB (roughly 1,000x the acoustic energy of an 80dB human shout)**. The 3,000Hz band cuts above low-frequency wind, water, and engine rumble while diffracting through concrete voids, and the **3-blast / 1-minute listen** cycle cuts oxygen expenditure by over 80%.

steps.title: Step 4: Aim Daylight SOS Sun Flashes 10km Away Using a Mirror or Phone Screen and V-Finger Sight
steps.description:
1. **Hold a Mirror, Dark Phone Screen, or Foil Plate Near Your Eye**: In daylight when you spot a distant search helicopter, ship, or ridge, hold a **small mirror (or switched-off black phone screen / flat foil board)** in one hand right beside your cheek and eye.
2. **Extend Your Other Arm to Form a V-Finger Rear Sight**: Stretch your opposite arm straight out in front of you, spread your **index and middle fingers into a V-shape**, and place the distant **target (helicopter, boat, or ridge)** right in the center of the V-notch.
3. **Overlap the Reflected Sun Spot onto Your V-Fingers**: Tilt the mirror slightly until the **bright reflected sun spot lands directly on the inner tips of your outstretched V-fingers**; this aligns your eye, V-finger sight, and target in a straight line so the beam hits the target 10km away.
4. **Wiggle the Beam in Morse SOS (3 Short · 3 Long · 3 Short)**: Keeping the sun spot centered on your V-fingers, flick your mirror wrist slightly to flash **3 short, 3 long, and 3 short pulses (··· --- ···)**, and sweep the horizon periodically even if no aircraft is visible yet.
steps.actionNote: > Why waving a mirror randomly toward the sky fails to alert a helicopter flying right past you: A reflected solar beam is only 0.5 degrees wide, so without a sight line it misses the aircraft by hundreds of meters; you must align the sun spot across your V-fingers onto the target.
svgLabels: Hold mirror, phone screen, or foil near eye
Frame distant target inside V-finger sight

deepDive.title: 0.5-Degree Specular Solar Beam Divergence and Three-Point V-Finger Optical Collimation Geometry
deepDive.text: Sunlight specularly reflected from a flat mirror or tempered phone glass diverges at only **0.5 degrees (the sun's angular diameter)**, maintaining **millions of candelas of flash intensity at 10–15km**. Because this narrow beam is invisible from the side, superimposing **the eye-adjacent mirror, the reflected spot on the outstretched V-finger notch, and the distant target** creates a 3-point collimated sight line accurate within 0.2 degrees.

fatalMistake.title: FATAL // Never put unground razor-sharp can edges to your mouth, and never hold a continuous mirror glare on an aircraft cockpit for tens of seconds
fatalMistake.description: Freshly cut beverage can edges are as sharp as razor blades and will slice your lips and tongue if blown before stone grinding. If you cut your hand while crafting, flush the wound immediately with [Oral Rehydration Salts & 0.9% Wound Saline](/protocol-24) and apply pressure using [Branch Splint & Boiled Burlap Hemostasis](/protocol-18). In dusty rubble, cover your nose with a [Charcoal & Sand Smoke Mask](/protocol-15) or wet cloth and blow the whistle instead of shouting to avoid dust inhalation. When signaling aircraft with a mirror, never lock continuous glare on the cockpit, which can blind the pilot; flash brief 3-pulse bursts and pause.
fatalMistake.consequence: Strictly follow the 4 rules: Stone-grind all cut metal edges + Seal both side holes with fingers + Blow 3 blasts then listen 1 min + Flash intermittent V-sighted SOS beams.

faqs.question: What can I use to make a 120dB emergency whistle if there are no empty beverage cans around?
faqs.causeDiagnostic: Any small hollow cavity paired with a narrow air slit can generate the same high-frequency Helmholtz resonance.
faqs.resolution: Use a **hollowed ballpoint pen barrel, an acorn cap, a hollow bamboo or reed node, or a bottle cap**. Hold an acorn cap or bottle cap tightly between the knuckles of both thumbs, form a tiny V-shaped gap between your thumbs, and blow sharply across the rim to produce a 110dB+ high-pitched rescue whistle.

faqs.question: How do I reflect sunlight toward a rescue helicopter in front of me when the sun is directly behind my back?
faqs.causeDiagnostic: When the sun is behind you, a single mirror held in front of your face is blocked by your own head and body shadow.
faqs.resolution: Use the **two-mirror relay method** by holding **two reflective surfaces (e.g., a dead smartphone screen in one hand and a mirror or foil board in the other)**. Catch the sunlight from behind your shoulder with the first reflector and bounce it onto the second mirror held beside your eye, then aim through your finger sight toward the target across 360 degrees.

shortsScript.hook: Trapped in rubble or stranded in the wild? Shouting ruins your voice and drains your stamina in 15 minutes! Here is how to call rescuers 10km away with an empty can and a mirror!
shortsScript.body: Cut a finger-width strip from an empty beverage can and grind the sharp edges smooth on a rock. Fold the top flat into a narrow air channel, and roll the bottom around a twig into a pencil-thick cylinder with a rice-grain sound gap. Seal both side holes tightly with your thumb and index finger and blow 3 short blasts to unleash a 120dB high-frequency shriek that cuts through storm noise for 2km! In daylight, hold a mirror or dead phone screen near your eye, overlap the reflected sun spot across a V-finger sight onto a rescue helicopter, and flash SOS up to 10km away!
